newsitem.title: USA: U.S. annoyed at Rafsanjani visit to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. annoyed at Rafsanjani visit to Turkey.

text.p: The United States Friday expressed disapproval of a visit by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani to NATO member Turkey and advised Ankara against improving ties with Tehran.
The four-day visit, which began Thursday, is aimed at boosting trade links between the two countries in defiance of U.S. efforts to isolate Iran.
"We don't think much" of the visit, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters. "We strongly advise the Turkish government not to improve its relationship with Iran."
Burns also expressed concern over reports that the two countries might try to increase military cooperation.
"For a NATO ally to even think of enhancing its military cooperation with Iran is quite unusual and is a great disappointment to us," Burns said.
"Iran is a country that is seeking a nuclear weapons capability. It's also a country that is funding and directing terrorism against NATO Western targets in Europe and North America."
Turkish President Suleyman Demirel said Thursday the talks with Rafsanjani would include matters of order, security and "the struggle against terrorism."
Turkey's relations with Iran have been one of several sources of friction between the United States and Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.

Washington expressed annoyance over a $23 billion agreement which Turkey signed in August for the supply of Iranian natural gas over 23 years, although U.S. officials said they doubted the deal would come to fruition.
